page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.large is a burstable virtual machine instance within the ecs.t5 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and runs on a KVM hypervisor, powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs, which correspond to 1 physical core with 2 threads, and 2.0 GiB of system memory. This instance does not feature any local SSD storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower-tier performance bracket. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1078.28, while the multi-core score reached 2088.79, reflecting its burstable CPU allocation model. Memory bandwidth tests showed a read-only small block cached speed of 145.07 GB/sec, dropping to 15.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write speed of 13.96 GB/sec. These metrics, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 2509.4, indicate that the hardware is optimized for low-intensity operations rather than sustained high-throughput computing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.t5-c1m1.large offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that experience sporadic activity. Because CPU resources are burstable, the instance is highly economical for tasks that remain idle most of the time but require occasional processing power. However, the lack of bundled local storage and low memory density of 1.0 GiB per vCPU represent clear tradeoffs, making it unsuitable for memory-intensive or storage-heavy applications.

This instance is best suited for light, non-critical workloads. Appropriate use cases include development and testing environments, low-traffic static web serving, small-scale Redis caching, and basic microservices that do not require sustained CPU performance or high network throughput.
